Get started with zuslothdb

Source: vignettes/zuslothdb.Rmd
zuslothdb.Rmd

zuslothdb runs SQL over local files from R. It compiles the experimental SlothDB engine into the package and puts a DBI driver on top, so there is no server, no system library and no download. This page connects, queries one CSV file, and shows how the package handles types, failures and writing.

library(DBI)
library(zuslothdb)

cars <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(mtcars, cars, row.names = FALSE)

Connect and query a file

zuslothdb() is a DBI driver, used the way duckdb::duckdb() is: code moves between the two by changing the first argument of dbConnect(). The engine reads files through SQL table functions, so there is no import step.

con <- dbConnect(zuslothdb(), dbdir = ":memory:")

dbGetQuery(con, paste0(
  "SELECT cyl, count(*) AS n, avg(mpg) AS mpg ",
  "FROM read_csv(", dbQuoteString(con, cars), ") GROUP BY cyl ORDER BY cyl"
))

# Open: what zuslothdb_read() returns and whether it takes reader options (Q12)
zuslothdb_read(con, cars)

Values arrive as R types, or not at all

Every engine type maps to one R type, and a value that would lose information is an error instead of a rounded number. A 64-bit integer is a double by default; beyond 2^53 you choose a wider type when connecting.

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT DATE '2026-11-17' AS day, 42::BIGINT AS n")

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT 9007199254740993::BIGINT AS n")
# a zuslothdb_type_error

con64 <- dbConnect(zuslothdb(), bigint = "integer64")
dbGetQuery(con64, "SELECT 9007199254740993::BIGINT AS n")
dbDisconnect(con64)

Failures are classed conditions

The engine never takes the R session down: its errors come back as conditions that inherit from zuslothdb_error, so a caller can tell a bad query from a missing feature. SlothDB has no prepared statements, so parameters are refused in v0.1.0.

tryCatch(
  dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT no_such_column FROM read_csv('missing.csv')"),
  zuslothdb_sql_error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT ? AS x", params = list(1))
# a zuslothdb_unsupported error

Write tables and keep them

Data frames are written through the engine’s appender, and a file database persists them. A database file is tied to the package version that wrote it.

dbWriteTable(con, "cars", mtcars)
dbAppendTable(con, "cars", mtcars[1:3, ])

dbBegin(con)
dbExecute(con, "DELETE FROM cars WHERE cyl = 8")
dbRollback(con)

dbListTables(con)
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

Where next

The reference index lists every function. zuslothdb_info() reports the engine commit, the patches applied and the thread count.
